title: "Single-Parameter Gauge-Covariant Loop-Flow Control for Phase-Shifting Transformers and Meshed Converter Networks"
date: 2026-07-28
---

[Download PDF](../assets/phase-power.pdf){.btn .btn-primary} &nbsp; [Source](https://github.com/TheChaosBureau/phase-power)

## Abstract

An *active-phase link element* is a branch whose series phase offset is set
independently of its endpoint bus angles: a phase-shifting transformer (PST), a
UPFC or other FACTS device, a back-to-back voltage-source converter pair, a
dual-active-bridge DC interface, or a grid-forming inverter in a meshed
low-inertia fleet. Meshed networks containing such elements — the European
transmission system and its PST-coordinated border flows being the largest
deployed instance — carry a loop-level coordination degree of freedom currently
managed by four layered mechanisms, none of which closes the loop-local,
real-time gap between them.

This paper identifies loop-flow coordination as an instance of the
*actuated-edge regime* of cellular-sheaf coordination, and shows that the
cycle-space dimension $b_1(G) = m - n + c$ gives a tight two-sided bound on the
number of scalar feedback parameters required to asymptotically stabilize the
trivial-connection equilibrium — attained by a canonical per-cycle feedback law
driven by the loop holonomy, the gauge-invariant observable identified
physically with circulating reactive power.

## Scope

Simulation stage. Results are benchmarked against a Verboomen-class optimal
power flow baseline on IEEE test networks; there is no hardware or field
validation. Each numerical claim in the paper maps to its own validation script
in the repository.
